questions.q: What does Field-Level Security (FLS) control, per this lesson?
options: Whether a specific field is visible, read-only, or editable for a given user, independent of object- or record-level access
Whether a user can log into Salesforce at all
Which Role Hierarchy a user belongs to
Which license a user is assigned
questions.explain: FLS is per-field access control, one level finer than object- or record-level access.

questions.q: Can a user have full access to view and edit an Opportunity record while one specific field on it is hidden from them?
options: Yes -- FLS can hide a single field independently, without hiding the record or the object
No -- hiding any field always hides the entire record
No -- FLS can only apply to entire objects, never individual fields
Yes, but only if the user's license is a Platform license
questions.explain: The lesson's core example is exactly this: full record access, one field hidden via FLS.

questions.q: Where is Field-Level Security configured, per this lesson?
options: On a Profile (as part of its baseline) or a Permission Set (as an additive grant) -- the same mechanisms from Lesson 28
Only directly on the individual field, with no connection to Profiles or Permission Sets
Only in the Role Hierarchy
Only through a Sharing Rule
questions.explain: FLS uses the same Profile/Permission Set mechanism as object-level access, just at a finer grain.

questions.q: What actually happens when a user queries or reports on a field that's hidden from them by FLS, per this lesson?
options: No error -- the field simply doesn't appear, or shows no value, with no indication FLS is the cause
Salesforce throws a clear permissions-denied error every time
The entire report fails to run
The user is automatically logged out of Salesforce
questions.explain: The lesson stresses this is a silent effect -- no error, just an absent or blank field value.

questions.q: If a report seems to be 'missing data' in a column you know is fully populated in the underlying object, what does this lesson say to check first?
options: Field-Level Security on that specific user's Profile or Permission Set
Whether the object was deleted
Whether the user's password has expired
Whether the org has exceeded its data storage limit
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly recommends checking FLS before assuming a data quality problem.
